Chief Executive’s Monthly Management Report – 31st May 2026
 
 
A Chara,  
 
I enclose the above report for your statutory consideration, this report has also been prepared under Section 136 & 
138 of the Local Government Act, 2001. The attached report is the Chief Executive’s Monthly Management Report for 
May 2026, detailing activities, updates, and progress across various departments of Louth County Council.  
 
The Corrs Civic Reception demonstrated the value of a strong cross-directorate approach, delivered through 
collaboration between Dundalk BIDs, the Museum and Corporate Services. The event showcased the collective 
capacity of Louth and the Council with all its partners to deliver a high-quality occasion that reflected positively on both 
Dundalk and County Louth as a great place to live, work and play, am I take this opportunity to sincerely thank all 
involved.. 
 
Here is a summary of some key achievements and actions from the Chief Executive Report for May 2026: 
 
1. Finance and System Support Directorate 
• 
Financial Management: 
o 
Expenditure to 27 May 2026: €70.7 million (35% of annual budget spent). 
o 
Income to 27 May 2026: €83.7 million (41% of annual budget invoiced). 
• 
ICT: 
o 
761 IT support calls logged; 85% resolved & 18% of inbound emails flagged as potentially harmful. 
o 
13,518 unique website page views; planning/maps, services, library, and housing most visited. 
o 
Cybersecurity training focused on AI-driven phishing threats. 
2. Economic Delivery Directorate 
• 
Tourism: 
o 
Strong presence at Balmoral Show and National Tourism Conference. 
o 
Louth venues secured €76,000 under the Grassroots Venue Support Scheme. 
• 
Local Enterprise Office: 
o 
Supported student enterprise awards, regional food showcases, and AI adoption events. 
o 
52 business advice clinics, 22 mentors, and 5 training courses delivered in May. 
• 
Planning: 
o 
102 planning applications received in April; 45 determined. 
o 
17 planning enforcement complaints investigated in April. 
o 
Living City Initiative extended to Dundalk and Drogheda for urban regeneration. 
3. Operations & Environment Delivery Directorate 
• 
Roads and Maintenance: 
o Extensive gully cleaning, drainage, and repairs across Dundalk, Ardee, Drogheda, and rural areas. 
o Regular road sweeping, footpath upgrades, and signage maintenance. 
• 
Environment: 
o 
340 litter investigations, 109 waste complaints YTD. 
o 
3 diesel laundering waste callouts in May (cost: €31,050). 
• 
Climate Action: 
o 
€651,374 allocated to 17 community climate projects.

Animal Control:

6 registered dog breeding establishments. 
• 
Fire & Emergency Services: 
o 
511 incidents YTD (down from 658 last year). 
o 
New fire appliances received and training centre developments underway. 
• 
Civil Defence: 
o 
Ongoing training and medical cover at community events.

Corporate

5. Housing & Culture Delivery Directorate 
• 
Housing:

353 people presented as homeless (13 April–12 May); 47 placed in emergency accommodation. 
o 
286 housing allocations YTD; 4741 on housing list, 63 relet/void properties as of 22 May. 
o 
828 maintenance requests received in May; 727 completed. 
o

o 
414 vacant property grant applications submitted; 314 approved. 
• 
Cultural Services: 
o 
Archives: New photo album of Ardee House acquired. 
o 
Libraries: 50 Spring into Storytime events, 1,171 participants. 
o 
Arts: Public art commissions, exhibitions, and creative events ongoing. 
o 
Museum: County quiz, workshops, and commencement of the strategy development Plan for 2026-
2030. 
6. Major Capital Projects & Infrastructure Delivery Directorate 
• 
Placemaking & Urban Regeneration: 
o 
URDF replaced by TCRIF; applications for Westgate (Drogheda) and St. Nicholas Quarter (Dundalk) 
submitted. 
o 
Ongoing engagement with property owners to address vacancy. 
• 
Physical Development: 
o 
Major projects: Narrow Water Bridge, N53 upgrade, Boyne Enterprise Link Road, and PANCR Phase 
2 progressing. 
o 
Greenways: Dundalk Bay to Carlingford public consultation completed. 
o 
Flood defence and coastal protection works ongoing in Dundalk, Drogheda, Carlingford, and Ardee. 
o 
School projects and active travel initiatives advancing, though some delayed due to budget 
constraints. 
 
I would like to conclude by expressing my sincere appreciation for the exceptional commitment, resilience, and 
professionalism demonstrated by the entire Louth County Council team.  
I encourage all members to read the report in full, which reflects the breadth, depth and impact of the remarkable work 
carried out across the organisation.

ArcGIS Online – Planning Applications Map Viewer 
 
The Planning Applications Mapping application continues to receive many visitors. The data in the system is 
updated regularly to update information on the publicly available system. It is available on the Graveyard 
Section of www.louthcoco.ie - E-Planning 
 
 
 
There were 3,082 views of the application between 01/05/2026 and 27/05/2026, an average of 119 views a day 
in May. 
 
 
Cyber Security Training  
 
May’s Cyber Security training highlighted that AI is making phishing attacks more sophisticated and targeted, 
enabling highly convincing emails that are difficult to detect and often aimed at specific staff or leadership. It 
reinforced that traditional warning signs are less reliable, so staff must remain vigilant—verifying requests, 
avoiding embedded links, and reporting suspicious activity—while the organisation continues to strengthen 
access controls and staff awareness as key defences.

The Living City Initiative (LCI) has been extended to 
include the urban centres of Dundalk and Drogheda.  
The scheme provides tax relief for qualifying 
expenditure on the refurbishment or conversion of 
certain buildings where special conditions are met.  
Its primary objective is to revitalise these areas by 
encouraging regeneration and bringing renewed 
activity and vibrancy into town centres.  
 
The LCI offers four types of tax relief for money 
spent on: 
1. Refurbishing or converting homes for owner-
occupiers. 
2. Refurbishing or converting homes rental 
properties (landlords). 
3. Upgrading 
commercial 
properties, 
with 
accelerated tax allowances for refurbishment 
or conversion. 
4. Living over the shop relief. 
 
This scheme helps regenerate older urban areas 
and supports the creation of refurbished residential 
homes in central locations.  Qualifying property 
owners can claim tax relief on refurbishment money 
spent - either through income tax (for an owner-
occupied residence) or as capital allowance for 
rental property. 
 
To date there have been a number of queries to the 
Council by property owners and 6 applications for 
the LCI scheme have been received by the team.
